questions.solution:

questions.question: The given bar graph shows the turnover of five companies (in crores). What is the difference between the average sales turnover of all the companies put together between the years 2018-2019 and 2019-2020?
questions.questionHtml:
The given bar graph shows the turnover of five companies (in crores).
 


What is the difference between the average sales turnover of all the companies put together between the years 2018-2019 and 2019-2020?
questions.solution:
Given:

Sales turnover data for the companies for the years 2018-2019 and 2019-2020 (in crores):

HDFC: 2018-19 = 250, 2019-20 = 300

GM: 2018-19 = 350, 2019-20 = 250

HERO: 2018-19 = 275, 2019-20 = 300

LG: 2018-19 = 200, 2019-20 = 300

BPL: 2018-19 = 400, 2019-20 = 350

Formula used:

Average sales turnover = (Sum of sales turnover for all companies) / Number of companies

Calculations:

For 2018-2019:

Total turnover for 2018-2019 = 250 + 350 + 275 + 200 + 400 = 1475

Average turnover for 2018-2019 = 1475 / 5 = 295

For 2019-2020:

Total turnover for 2019-2020 = 300 + 250 + 300 + 300 + 350 = 1500

Average turnover for 2019-2020 = 1500 / 5 = 300

Difference in average turnover:

Difference = 300 - 295 = 5

The difference in average sales turnover between the years 2018-2019 and 2019-2020 is 5 crores.

questions.question: Study the given graph and answer the question that follows. The total number of computers of type A sold in January and May is what percentage less than the total number of computers of type B sold from March to May? (correct to one decimal place)

questions.solution:
Calculation:

Total number of computers of type A sold in January and May = (250 + 350)

⇒ 600

Total number of computers of type B sold from March to May = (350 + 325 + 425)

Required percentage = [(1100 – 600)/1100 × 100]

⇒ (500/1100 × 100)

questions.question: Study the graph which shows the target and actual production of ACs, (in thousands) of a factory over five months and answer the question that follows. The total target production of ACs in February, March, April, and May is what percent less than the total actual production of ACs over five months? (correct to one decimal place)
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Total target production of ACs in February, March, April and May = 30 + 80 + 90 + 100 = 300(in thousands)

Total actual production of ACs over five months = 70 + 50 + 100 + 80 + 120 = 420(in thousands)

Required % = 120/420 × 100 = 28.57% ∼ 28.6%

The production of sugar by company Q in 2016 = 75

The production of sugar by company Q in 2017 = 90

​The percentage rise in the production of sugar in 2017 by company Q as compares to the previous year 2016 = [(90 – 75)/75 × 100]

⇒ (15/75 × 100) = 20%

Now,

The production of sugar by company Q in 2017 = 90

The production of sugar by company Q in 2018 = 100

​The percentage rise in the production of sugar in 2018 by company Q as compares to the previous year 2017 = [(100 – 90)/90 × 100]

Now,

The production of sugar by company Q in 2018 = 100

The production of sugar by company Q in 2019 = 115

​The percentage rise in the production of sugar in 2019 by company Q as compares to the previous year 2018 = [(115 – 100)/100 × 100]

questions.question: Study the given histogram and answer the questions that follow. The histogram shows the distribution of marks obtained by 115 students in a college. A student is marked as qualified if he/she obtains marks above 40.5. Here, the ratio of the number of qualified students to that of students who are not qualified is:
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given histogram and answer the questions that follow.

The histogram shows the distribution of marks obtained by 115 students in a college.

A student is marked as qualified if he/she obtains marks above 40.5. Here, the ratio of the number of qualified students to that of students who are not qualified is:
questions.solution:
Calculate the number of qualified students (marks above 40.5)

Marks 40.5 to 50.5: Frequency = 2.5 × 10 = 25

Marks 50.5 to 60.5: Frequency = 3.0 × 10 = 30

Marks 60.5 to 70.5: Frequency = 2.0 × 10 = 20

Marks 70.5 to 80.5: Frequency = 1.0 × 10 = 10

Marks 80.5 to 90.5: Frequency = 1.0 × 10 = 10

Total number of qualified students = 25 + 30 + 20 + 10 + 10 = 95

Calculate the number of non-qualified students (marks ≤ 40.5)

Marks 20.5 to 30.5: Frequency = 0.5 × 10 = 5

Marks 30.5 to 40.5: Frequency = 1.5 × 10 = 15

Total number of non-qualified students = 5 + 15 = 20

Calculate the ratio of qualified to non-qualified students

⇒ Ratio = Number of qualified students / Number of non-qualified students

⇒ Ratio = 95 / 20 = 19 : 4

questions.question: Study the given graph and answer the question that follows. In the year 2019, if the imports increased by the same percentage as that in 2018 over its previous year, then what was the amount (in Rs. crores) of the imports in the year 2019?
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given graph and answer the question that follows.

In the year 2019, if the imports increased by the same percentage as that in 2018 over its previous year, then what was the amount (in Rs. crores) of the imports in the year 2019?
questions.solution:
Alternate MethodThe percentage can be converted into ratio.

Ratio of 2018 and 2017 = 450/400 = 9/8

The same ratio is for 2019 and 2018 = 9/8

⇒ x/450 = 9/8

⇒ x = (450 × 9)/8 = 506.25

Traditional method:

Given:

Imports in 2017 = Rs.400 crores

Imports in 2018 = Rs.450 crores

Formula used:

Percentage increase of imports = Increase over previous year/Imports of current year × 100 

Calculation:

Percentage increase of imports of the year 2018 = (450 - 400)/450 × 100 

⇒ 100/9 %

Let the imports in the year 2019 be = y 

As per the question; Percentage increase of imports in 2019 = Percentage increase of imports in 2018 

⇒ Percentage increase of imports in 2019 = 100/9 % 

⇒ (y - Imports in 2018)/y ×100 = 100/9 

⇒ (y - 450)/y = 1/9 

⇒ y = 9 × (y - 450)

⇒ y - 9y = - 9 × 450 

⇒ - 8y = - 9 × 450 

⇒ y = 9 × 450/8 

⇒ y = 506.25

∴ The imports in the year 2019 was of Rs.506.25 crores.

questions.question: In the given histogram, in which class interval, the median lies?
questions.questionHtml: In the given histogram, in which class interval, the median lies?
questions.solution:
If number of the observation is n is odd, then the median is [(n + 1)/2]th observation.

If number of the observation is n is even, then the median will be the average of the (n/2)th and [(n/2 + 1)]th observation.

Total number of students = 50 + 70 + 85 + 90 + 60 + 45 = 400

Median = [(400/2) + (400/2) + 1)]2 = (200 + 201)/2 = 200.5th (201th) students (which comes in 60 - 70)

Number of students who lies (40 - 50) = 50 students

Number of students who lies (50 - 60) = 70 students = 51th to 120th

Number of students who lies (60 - 70) = 85 students = 121th to 205th

So, 200.5th (201th) students comes in 60 - 70.
